VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The base case \(n=0\) and the inductive step from \(k\) to \(k+1\) are correctly treated.  In the sum index shift the boundary terms \(j=0\) and \(j=k+1\) are separately identified as having coefficient \(1\), matching \(\binom{k+1}{0}=\binom{k+1}{k+1}=1\).  The interior coefficients are combined by Pascal’s rule for \(1\le j\le k\); the required addition \(\iota(a)+\iota(b)=\iota(a+b)\) is used only where both binomial coefficients are \(\ge 1\), so the cited \(\text{lem-of-naturals-positive}\) (which states additivity for \(m,n\ge 1\)) is sufficient.  No division by zero or out‑of‑range binomial coefficient occurs.  The induction covers every \(n\in\mathbb N\).

Their statements and boundary conventions support the proof as used.
